listings.content: Once a leather daddy bar, this has turned into one of the newer hip bars in the area.

listings.name: Akbar
listings.content: It's long been popular with a mixed crowd for its decent drinks and good jukebox. The hot and sweaty dance club in the back room brings in the hip gay crowd.
listings.price: No cover for the bar, $3 for the back room

listings.name: El Cid
listings.content: Very mediocre Mexican food and tapas, but more popular for the rock/punk shows that it hosts at night.

listings.name: Gold Room
listings.content: Divey bar with a mix of Echo Park hipsters and Latino immigrants. The interior looks like the inside of a limo from the 80s. On certain nights they offer $5 beer+tequila shot specials.

listings.name: The Guest House
listings.content: Former coffee house turned beer and cocktail sipping place.

listings.name: Red Lion Tavern
listings.content: Kitchy Bavarian-style pub that serves sausages and steins of German beer. Downstairs is darker and more mellow; upstairs is more raucous with a great outdoor patio. Large enough that it's good for long, private conversations.

listings.name: The Short Stop
listings.content: Once popular with off-duty cops, the Echo Park trendophiles have taken it over in the last few years. One of the best jukeboxes in the city with a variety from rock, current/classic hip-hop, 80s, Hi-NrG, country, etc. The bar is owned by Greg Dulli, former lead singer of the Afghan Whigs and now The Twilight Singers.

listings.name: Tiki Ti
listings.content: "Tiki-tastic" this tiny tiki bar is full of all the fun and booze a tiki bar should have.

listings.name: Ye Rustic Inn
listings.content: Friendly Los Feliz dive bar with strong drinks and a good mix of people. They also have a pretty solid food menu with tasty wings. Can get loud and crowded on weekends.

listings.name: Black Cat
listings.content: Upscale American gastropub in a historic location related to the LGBTQ civil rights movement.

listings.name: Holiday Inn Express Downtown West
listings.content: A block from MacArthur Park.

listings.name: Drum Barracks Civil War Museum
listings.content: Museum preserving the last remaining Civil War military post in Southern California.

listings.name: Phineas Banning House
listings.content: 19th-century estate belonging to Phineas Banning. Museum includes a large display of 19th century stagecoaches located in the barn and a one-room school house adjacent to the house. Resting place for visiting ship's captains. Banning's backyard is now a city park, Banning Park.

listings.name: Best Western Los Angeles Worldport Hotel
Holiday Inn Los Angeles Gateway - Torrance by IHG
Red Roof Inn Los Angeles – Wilmington, CA
Motel 6 Harbor City, CA - Los Angeles
Museum of Contemporary Art
listings.content: The permanent collection is fairly interesting, but the changing exhibitions can be more hit or miss. The museum has no 'traditional' art, so bring an open mind. As of 1/11/2020 admission is now free to everyone.The gift shop is fun for at least 20 minutes of wonder and awe.

listings.name: The Broad
listings.content: A newer contemporary art museum built to house the collection of billionaire philanthropist Eli Broad (pronounced "brode"). Opened in September 2015, the museum has a collection of almost 2,000 pieces of postwar and contemporary art, with some of the most famous names of modernism represented (Warhol, Lichtenstein, etc.). The building is a spectacular example of architecture, with a honeycomb-like exterior and visitors entering the third floor exhibit galleries via tunnels through a concrete "vault" that holds most of the museum's collections.
listings.price: Free; entry by timed ticket only, advance reservation recommended. Special exhibitions require fee

listings.name: Angels Flight
listings.content: Historic funicular railway

listings.name: Cathedral of Our Lady of the Angels
listings.content: This large and austere cathedral, dedicated to Saint Vibiana, is the head of the Archdiocese of Los Angeles. It was opened in 2002 at a cost of nearly $200 million, replacing The Cathedral of St Vibiana which was heavily damaged in the 1994 earthquake.

listings.name: Los Angeles Central Public Library
listings.content: The huge central library, completed in 1926 and refurbished in the 1990s, is a remarkable Art Deco structure surrounded by a pleasant garden with pools and fountains. Inside is a monumental rotunda with elaborate murals and decorations, while most of the stacks are housed in the newer Tom Bradley Wing on the east side of the building, with its glass-roofed atrium. The library almost always has a public exhibition going, usually showing off local art or historical artifacts.

listings.name: 2nd Street Tunnel
listings.content: A somewhat obscure but very recognizable landmark is this tunnel, built in the 1920s beneath Bunker Hill and lined with glossy white tiles that bathe the tunnel in a soft glow. If you don't recognize it from one of the many films shot here (Blade Runner, The Terminator, Independence Day, Kill Bill Vol. 1 and many, many others), chances are you've seen it in at least one of the dozens (possibly even hundreds) of car commercials that have made use of its unique lighting scheme. The Figueroa Street entrance is the more attractive (and recognizable) one; the tunnel looks considerably grittier on the other side.

listings.name: U.S. Bank Tower
listings.content: At 73 floors and 1,017, this was for a time the tallest building in the Western United States. And while it has been surpassed in height by the Wilshire Grand tower, it still dominates the Los Angeles skyline. It used to have an indoor and an open-air observation deck, the OUE Skyspace, on the 70th floor, with a glass slide on the outside between floors 70 and 69, but it has been permanently closed since 2020. Note to photographers: the building's security personnel will try to discourage you from taking pictures of this building if you're on the grounds of the tower, but as long as you are standing on a public sidewalk you may legally take as many pictures of the building as you like.

listings.name: Wilshire Grand Center
listings.content: Completed in 2017, this skyscraper has claimed the title of tallest building in Los Angeles, owing to the tall mast atop the structure. A sail-shaped roof tops the building, which is brightly illuminated at night. A hotel occupies most of the building, with the top four floors holding restaurants and bars including a rooftop bar perched on the 73rd floor.

listings.name: Music Center and Disney Hall
listings.content: Impressive music hall architecture, with public tours available most days. The Dorothy Chandler Pavilion is open to the public Christmas Eve day with almost round the clock performances by amateur cultural arts groups. The Walt Disney Concert Hall has daily tours; check website for schedules.

listings.name: Walt Disney Concert Hall
listings.content: One of four halls of the Los Angeles Music Center, it is where the Los Angeles Philharmonic and Los Angeles Master Chorale perform.
listings.image: Image-Disney Concert Hall by Carol Highsmith edit.jpg

listings.name: Ahmanson Theater
listings.content: One of four halls of the Los Angeles Music Center, it is the primary venue for theatrical runs in Downtown Los Angeles.

listings.name: Mark Taper Forum
listings.content: The most intimate of the four halls of the Los Angeles Music Center, it serves as Los Angeles' venue for experimental theater.

listings.name: Dorothy Chandler Pavilion
listings.content: One of four halls of the Los Angeles Music Center, it serves as the venue for the Los Angeles Opera and Dance at the Music Center.
listings.image: Dorothy Chandler Pavilion, LA, CA, jjron 22.03.2012.jpg

listings.name: Engine Co. No. 28
listings.content: Comfort food at its best. A restored actual fire station that churns out great meatloaf, fried chicken and lemonade, all in an elegant atmosphere with great service.

listings.name: Kendall's Brasserie
listings.content: Great French menu at a perfect location to catch any of the great evening programs at the surrounding venues. Whatever you order, do not miss their French Fries!

listings.name: Nick and Stef's
listings.content: Fantastic steak house, run by the Patina restaurant empire. If you like beef, this is some of the best in town, with a glass-enclosed aging room where you can view the meat as it ages. Try the dry-aged Ribeye, it will make your head spin. They also have 12 kinds of potatoes on the menu. Not sure why, but they're all good. In the Wells Fargo Center, across from MOCA.

listings.name: Water Grill
listings.content: Excellent seafood and service. Perhaps a bit pricey, but elegant and wonderful.

listings.name: Elevate Lounge @ Penthouse
listings.content: Excellent views of the city.

listings.name: Gallery Bar
listings.content: Upscale cocktail lounge. House drink is the Black Dahlia cocktail, named for the famed victim of the notorious murder, who was last seen wandering through the hotel.

listings.name: Library Bar
listings.content: An upscale pub style bar with a floor-to-ceiling and wall-to-wall library that houses a wide range of literary classics, while playing great music from Jim Hendrix to The Who. Knowledgeable bartenders offer an extensive beer selection and cocktails that are both classic and innovative.

listings.name: The Rooftop Bar @ The Standard
listings.content: This unique bar offers a hipster hangout with excellent views of the city from thirteen stories up. Wear warm clothes during cold weather, and be prepared for drink prices in the $10+ range for mixed drinks. Don't forget to try the waterbeds or even jump in their pool for a swim.

listings.name: Seven Grand
listings.content: Popular whiskey bar owned by the owner of the Golden Gopher and Broadway Bar.

listings.name: Spire 73 at Intercontinental Hotel Downtown
listings.content: Tallest open air bar in USA at the top of the Intercontinental Hotel Downtown Los Angeles in the Wilshire Grand Building. Bar and Restaurant with amazing views of Los Angeles at about 1000 high.

listings.name: Omni
listings.content: The jury for the OJ Simpson trial in 1995 was sequestered here. Convenient to MOCA, Disney Concert Hall, upscale Noe Restaurant and Bar is onsite.

listings.name: Hilton Checkers
listings.content: AAA Four diamond, renovated 1920s luxury hotel. Weekend packages are offered.

listings.name: Millennium Biltmore
listings.content: The grand-daddy of all downtown hotels, with its gorgeous lobby and fancy restaurants.

listings.name: The Standard
listings.content: Trendy hotel with designer rooms and a bar and swimming pool on the roof. There is also a West Hollywood location.

listings.name: Westin Bonaventure
listings.content: Recognizable from various movies it has appeared in.
